$comment: One synthetic event, dumped from disruptions/api/notification_api.py's `_synthetic_event` -- the body `POST /notification-api/v1/test-events` actually signs and sends. It is a GENERATED file, not an authored one: regenerate it rather than editing it, with the recipe under `how_to_regenerate`. It exists because a hand-written transcription of that function drifted from it in eight fields (the vendored receiver's end-to-end fixture, corrected 2026-09-09), and nothing caught the drift -- `payload.call` and `payload.probabilities` are deliberately OPEN objects in event.schema.json, so a wrongly named key inside them is schema-VALID. Stop places and ids here are test values and name no real client.

how_to_regenerate.why: A client's first sight of a real payload is a test event, so a fixture that teaches `probabilities.cancel` or `call.aimed_departure` -- neither of which any producer emits -- breaks their receiver on the first genuine cancelled train, in production, at go-live.
how_to_regenerate.the_other_producer: disruptions/api/varsel.py::_webhook_payload builds the payload of a REAL event, and test_notification_api.py::test_the_synthetic_payload_has_the_same_shape_as_a_real_one compares the two in both directions. So pinning against this file pins against both.
how_to_regenerate.checked_by: disruptions/api/test_notification_api.py::test_the_committed_test_event_sample_still_matches_the_producer rebuilds this event from `_synthetic_event` under the inputs above and compares structure, leaf types, every non-derived top-level value and the three payload parts -- the way test_webhook_signing.py re-derives signing-vectors.json. A regenerated sample that drifts from the producer fails there before it can rot the way the fixture it replaced did.

how_to_consume.timestamps: `occurred_at`, `valid_until`, `call_date` and `payload.call.aimed_departure_time` are fixed instants from the generating run. A receiver test asserting on its own clock must re-stamp them and PRESERVE THE OFFSETS: `valid_until` is the earlier of occurred_at + 60 minutes and the departure, which here is the departure at occurred_at + 45 minutes.
how_to_consume.identity: `event_id`, `alert_id` and `journey_ref` are minted per call on that route (`test-<nonce>` / `KIX:Test:<nonce>`), deliberately, so two test events are never read as two revisions of one train. Substitute a nonce rather than reusing this one if a test sends more than once.
how_to_consume.phase: `confirmed`, and the whole event is coherent with it: both probabilities 1.0, every delay figure null, `effect: cancelled`. The supplied client's `defaultDisplay` maps `predicted` to `alert` and everything else to `silent`, so a receiver test built on this event asserts `silent`.
